name: Julian Ashcombe
equipment: Aramid vest, concealable, worn under a charcoal Savile Row suit that was cut to hide it
Snub-nose .38 revolver (S&W Model 36), 5 rounds loaded, which he dislikes and carries in an ankle holster
Cover passport: Julian Ashby, British, fine-art insurance assessor for a Lloyd's syndicate (excellent legend, real office, real switchboard)
Business cards in four names, two of them his
A gold Dunhill lighter with a hollow fuel chamber big enough for one roll of microfilm
Minox B subminiature camera and two cassettes of film
A slim leather diary of dinner engagements, half of them invented
A walking umbrella with a brass handle, from Swaine Adeney
Diners Club card in the name of Julian Ashby
The team's operational float: an envelope of Austrian schillings, Deutschmarks and Turkish lira (tracked as dollars in the wallet line)
features: Versatility (Human origin: +1 to all ability scores)
Silver Tongue (expertise, double proficiency bonus, on Persuasion and Deception checks)
Rally (bonus action: an ally who can hear him gains 1d6+3 temporary hit points and may end being frightened; 3 uses per long rest)
Read the Room (after 1 minute of conversation, learn one goal, fear or lie of the person he is talking to: his Insight vs their Deception)

Expense Account (Corporate background: he can get a meeting with almost any businessman, hotelier or minor official by telephone, and his legend's office will vouch for him during London business hours)

personality.traits: I am charming in the way some people are tall: I cannot switch it off and I have stopped apologising for it. I tip too much, remember every waiter's name, and listen to people as if they were the only person in the restaurant, which is usually a lie and occasionally true.
personality.ideals: Every person has a price, and almost none of them are money. Find the real one and you never need the gun.
personality.bonds: Sofia Varga pulled me out of a very bad evening in Trieste in 1980 and has never once mentioned it. I owe her a life and I intend to pay it before she needs it.
personality.flaws: I enjoy the lie. Not the necessity of it, the craft of it, and a man who enjoys the lie will one day tell one more than he needs to, to the wrong person, because it was beautiful.

appearance: A tall, fair, slightly too handsome Englishman of thirty-nine in a very good suit, with a public-school voice he can shift two classes in either direction at will. He stoops a little to talk to people, which makes them feel confided in. There is a white scar through his left eyebrow he explains differently every time. He smokes Rothmans he rarely finishes and uses the lighting of them to watch reflections in shop windows.
backstory: Julian Ashcombe spent eleven years selling paintings that were mostly real to people who were mostly honest, first in Bond Street and then in Geneva, before a quiet woman from the Foreign Office asked whether he might keep doing exactly that while noticing which Soviet trade attaches bought what, and with whose money. The Annex took him in 1979 as an access agent and kept him because he is, quite simply, the best cold-approach recruiter it has: he has turned a Bulgarian commercial counsellor over three lunches and a Czech cipher clerk over one very long night of Moravian wine. He is not a street man and knows it; he leaves the drops to Sofia and the guns to Callum. His fine-art insurance legend is the strongest in the team, which is why he carries the money. He has met Martin Vell's comms officer, Lionel Pryce, at six or seven station suppers, and likes him, and thinks he is wasted on telex.
